tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: 13 items from Nov 6 to Nov 24 that each cut LLM serving cost at a different layer, mostly arXiv papers plus Google's XLA Serving Engine launch and an AWS case study. Through Nov 19 the KV cache was the most-attacked target, ending with RoCoKV and TideCache.
whats_new: LoomKV (Nov 24) compresses the KV cache losslessly from GPU memory down to SSD on an unmodified serving engine, storing BF16 KV at 0.71x raw size and reporting 2.7-3.6x raw goodput on the AgentX trace.
why_it_matters: KV-cache memory is the dominant serving bottleneck in this thread (7 of 13 items), and LoomKV is the first entry that claims lossless savings without engine changes, so cache tiering may become a drop-in layer rather than a fork.

beats.headline: Serving stacks: XLA Serving Engine, edge simulation, cross-Region routing
beats.summary: Infrastructure that decides where and on what hardware requests run.

beats.headline: Fewer tokens and less traffic: VLM cropping, MoE activation deltas, shorter chain-of-thought
beats.summary: Cost cuts outside the cache: smaller visual inputs, compressed expert-parallel communication, and shorter reasoning training targets.

beats.headline: The KV cache becomes the main target
beats.summary: Six papers attack cache memory: intent-aware prefix reuse, verified compression, prefill/decode KV translation, Gemma 4 shared K=V storage, reasoning-trace compression, and hybrid-model cache streaming in SGLang.

beats.headline: LoomKV: lossless KV compression across GPU, CPU and SSD tiers
beats.summary: Stores BF16 KV at 0.71x raw size on an unmodified engine and reports 2.7-3.6x goodput past LMCache's LRU cliff.

open_questions: Do any of the KV-cache methods (RoCoKV, Verify Before You Fetch, BridgeKV, LoomKV) land in vLLM, SGLang or another mainstream serving engine?
Does LoomKV release code, and do its goodput gains hold on traces other than AgentX?
Does TideCache's SGLang implementation get merged upstream or released as code?
Does the Gemma 4 store-K=V-once trick ship in a paged serving engine release, and with what measured memory savings?
Does Google publish throughput or latency benchmarks for XLA Serving Engine against vLLM on the same hardware?
take_for_builders: If you offload KV cache with LMCache or similar, measure goodput as the working set crosses your LRU capacity before adding GPUs; that cliff is where LoomKV claims its gains.
